name: Green Anarchism
summary: Green anarchism combines the anarchist rejection of the state and hierarchy with an ecological critique, holding that states, capitalism and industrial production drive environmental destruction. It favours stateless, decentralised, bioregional or communal societies, degrowth, direct action and, in some strands, animal liberation. Strands divide mainly over technology and civilization: primitivists want to abandon agriculture and industry, while social ecologists keep reason, cities and technology under democratic control.
scope: The family as described in the Wikipedia overview, centred on John Zerzan's anarcho-primitivism and Murray Bookchin's social ecology, with deep ecology, green syndicalism and total liberation as further strands. Where primitivists and social ecologists disagree (foraging, population, consensus, technology), the answer is 0 or low confidence. Bookchin's later communalism and individualist or violent offshoots such as Kaczynski are not the mainstream represented.

sources.title: Green anarchism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Overview of strands, anti-state, anti-capitalist and degrowth positions, direct action, animal liberation.

sources.title: Future Primitive
sources.author: John Zerzan
sources.usedFor: Primitivist critique of civilization, agriculture, division of labour, domestication, time and symbolic culture.

sources.title: Anarcho-primitivism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Primitivist positions on technology, foraging, division of labour, sabotage and animals.

sources.title: Social Anarchism or Lifestyle Anarchism: An Unbridgeable Chasm
sources.author: Murray Bookchin
sources.usedFor: Social-ecology wing: assemblies and confederation, technology, capitalism, property, critique of primitivism and consensus.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Green anarchists reject state provision, yet most favour communal care and few oppose free health access; primitivists even question modern medicine, so the strands split.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: A statutory wage presupposes the state and wage labour, both of which green anarchists want abolished; inferred from their anti-state, anti-wage stance, not from any stated view.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Green anarchism is anti-capitalist and blames market-driven extraction and productivism for ecological damage; it also rejects state planning, but the market claim itself is firmly rejected.

public-ownership.rationale: Bookchin-style and syndicalist strands favour communal or workers' ownership rather than state ownership; an anti-state movement does not endorse public ownership by the state.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Taxation belongs to the state they want abolished, yet they are hostile to the wealthy and accumulation; the movement did not address tax policy so adherents split.

unions-good.rationale: Green syndicalists promote unions and workers' self-management, while primitivists reject industrial labour organisation altogether; the strands split.

property-fundamental.rationale: Bookchin endorses Kropotkin's call to abolish private property and the movement favours community ownership; a strong private-property right is rejected.

regulate-corporations.rationale: They want corporations abolished or dismantled rather than regulated by a state they distrust; inferred, with some support for restraining them in the meantime.

cut-welfare.rationale: They reject the state and the dependency of industrial society, but do not argue for cutting welfare as the right does; they would replace it with mutual aid, so mildly disagree.

worker-ownership.rationale: Green syndicalism promotes workers' self-management and councils, and Bookchin favours communal economic relations; primitivists reject the businesses altogether, so only mild agreement.

surveillance-ok.rationale: An anti-state movement opposes state surveillance; green radicals have been targets of it and reject the security justification.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Anarchists oppose state prohibition of what adults do, but the movement did not stress it; inferred from anti-state libertarianism.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Anarchists distrust state censorship, though many oppose hateful speech socially; inferred from anti-state principle.

strong-leader.rationale: Anarchism rejects hierarchy and rulers entirely, and Bookchin names hierarchy as the root of ecological and social problems.

state-harmful.rationale: Eco-anarchists see the rise of states as the main cause of environmental degradation and call for abolishing them.

limit-guns.rationale: They oppose state disarmament of the people, though they do not advocate gun culture; inferred from anti-state stance.

empower-police-military.rationale: Police and military are instruments of the state they seek to abolish.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Adherents split between anti-commodification and anti-state libertarian positions; sources do not address it.

decide-locally.rationale: Localism and bioregionalism are core, and Bookchin's municipal assemblies and confederation put power at the local level.

rehabilitation.rationale: Anarchists reject state punishment and prisons, and favour restorative or community responses; inferred, not documented in the sources.

traditional-family.rationale: Anarchism opposes hierarchy including patriarchy, and Bookchin names patriarchy as a hierarchy; primitivists idealise foraging band life but not the modern traditional family.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Many anarchists reject state marriage altogether, so they would not demand its extension; the issue is not addressed by the sources.

abortion-legal.rationale: Anti-hierarchy and anti-patriarchal stance implies bodily autonomy, though many would reject state regulation either way; inferred.

more-religion-public.rationale: Anarchists reject institutional hierarchy and green anarchists are generally secular, though deep ecology has spiritual strains; inferred.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Anti-hierarchy ethics imply opposing racial domination, but the sources do not describe a programme; they would favour direct, non-state remedies.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Ecofeminist and social-ecology strands stress social construction of domination, while primitivist and deep-ecology thinkers appeal to natural wholeness; split and unsourced.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: They want to replace nation-states with bioregions and communities, so national culture is not a goal; some value local and indigenous cultures.

gradual-change.rationale: Green anarchists favour direct action, sabotage and revolutionary change over respect for established institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Anarchists reject the state's borders; they do not treat immigration as something to cut, though bioregionalists stress rootedness; inferred.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: They oppose globalised capitalism and the state; the UN and similar bodies are superstates they reject.

free-trade.rationale: The movement opposes globalised capitalism and extractive trade; anti-globalisation protest is part of its history.

nation-first.rationale: They reject the nation-state and national interest as frames, and also globalised cooperation of states; they would reject the choice itself, leaning to disagree.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Anarchists oppose state military power; inferred, since the sources do not discuss intervention.

open-borders.rationale: Anarchists oppose the borders of states, but bioregionalists value place; inferred from anti-state principle.

limit-growth.rationale: Eco-anarchists oppose productivism and extractivism and call for degrowth and deindustrialisation.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: They demand radical change but reject government as its agent, so the statement, which asks for government action, splits them.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Primitivists call for abolishing technology; even Bookchin rejects technocratic ecology that relies on technological breakthroughs.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Radical environmentalists took direct action against nuclear infrastructure from the 1970s.

revolution-justified.rationale: Green anarchism aims at overthrowing the state and capitalism; Bookchin speaks of social revolution and insurrection as serious struggles.

experts-over-public.rationale: Bookchin rejects technocratic ecology, and anarchists reject rule by specialists; Zerzan traces hierarchy to specialisation.

central-planning.rationale: Anarchists reject centralised state planning; they favour decentralised production by free associations of producers.

socialized-markets.rationale: They favour communal production over markets, though some strands allow exchange; the sources discuss associations of producers, not markets.

land-value-tax.rationale: A state tax is not an anarchist remedy; the idea is unaddressed so inferred from anti-state stance.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Hostile to hereditary wealth, but taxation requires a state; unaddressed so adherents split.

basic-income.rationale: A state-paid income is at odds with abolishing the state and wage system; inferred, unaddressed.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Tariffs are state tools protecting industry, which they want to dismantle; they favour local self-reliance, so only mild disagreement.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The state steering industrial investment contradicts both anti-state and anti-industrial positions.

widespread-small-property.rationale: They reject private property in favour of common ownership but also dislike concentrated corporate power; primitivists reject property entirely.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies setting wages are state-run and wage-preserving; anarchists reject both.

one-party-rule.rationale: Single-party rule is the opposite of the stateless, non-hierarchical order they seek.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Anarchism rejects all hereditary or other rulers.

democracy-best.rationale: Bookchin demands direct democracy, while anarchists reject representative states and consensus anarchists reject majority rule; the statement's wording splits them.

direct-votes.rationale: Bookchin's assembly model features direct democracy over decisions; consensus-oriented strands prefer other methods, hence only mild agreement.

workers-councils.rationale: Green syndicalism promotes workers' councils, and Bookchin favours councils and assemblies, though he stresses municipal assemblies over workplace ones; primitivists differ.

right-to-secede.rationale: Decentralisation and bioregional federation imply that communities can withdraw from larger bodies; inferred from localism.

natural-rulers.rationale: Anarchism denies any natural entitlement to rule, as hierarchy is the source of domination.

political-violence-never.rationale: Earth First!, ALF and ELF practised sabotage and some factions attack; most strands reject strict pacifism though they differ on violence against people.

war-builds-character.rationale: Anarchists oppose war as a state activity, and Bookchin describes warlike societies critically.

separate-church-state.rationale: Anarchists reject the state, so separation follows by default; unaddressed in sources.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Anarchists reject state law and scriptural authority as hierarchy; deep ecology's spirituality is not scriptural.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Anarcho-capitalist private defence contradicts their anti-capitalism; green anarchists favour community arrangements.

military-superiority.rationale: They oppose militaries and state rivalry.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Green anarchists reject nation-states for bioregions and communities (s1), and Bookchin attacks xenophobia (s4); neither discusses ethnic nationhood as such.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Bookchin gives class struggle a central place alongside hierarchy while primitivists locate the origin in agriculture and civilization; the strands split.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Egalitarian and anti-hierarchical, but sources talk of abolishing hierarchy rather than equal outcomes; mild agreement inferred.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Indigenous land-based life is admired and rewilding and bioregionalism favour local control; documented as a preference mainly by primitivists and deep ecologists.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Unaddressed in the sources; anti-colonial but state-to-state payments sit badly with anti-statism.

civilizational-union.rationale: They reject civilization-states and supranational unions; civilization itself is the target for primitivists.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Green anarchists prize mutual aid and communal ownership and oppose competitive accumulation.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Anarchists stress mutual obligation and also individual freedom; not addressed in the sources.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Deep ecology's biocentrism rejects anthropocentrism and recognises value in nature itself; Bookchin's social ecology also values nature but in a more human-inclusive way.

limit-population.rationale: Deep ecologists proposed drastic population reduction, while Bookchin and social ecologists reject population control as a diversion from capitalism; the movement is split.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Anarcho-primitivists and most eco-anarchists hold industrial civilisation to be the cause of ecological destruction and alienation.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Green anarchism rejects technological acceleration, with primitivists wanting technology abolished.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anti-technology outlook makes enhancement suspect, though some anarchists value bodily autonomy; inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anarchists reject government, and rule by algorithms adds technological domination, which green anarchists oppose.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anarchists want to protect privacy from the state, though technology-averse strands avoid such tools; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Primitivists wish to return to a pre-agricultural life but not to an old social order; others seek a new non-hierarchical society.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Anarchists hold strong ideological commitments; not directly addressed in the sources.

direct-action.rationale: Direct action is central, from Earth First! monkeywrenching to the ALF and ELF.

means-match-ends.rationale: Anarchist prefigurative politics holds that methods should embody the aim; Bookchin discusses organisation reflecting the free society, but sources give this only implicitly.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Anarcho-primitivists want a return to hunter-gathering, while Bookchin and other eco-anarchists reject it as romantic; the family is genuinely split.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Primitivists seek to abolish specialisation, and Kropotkin's criticism of the mental-manual division is cited by eco-anarchists; Bookchin accepts some specialisation, so mild agreement.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Kropotkin's communist anarchism, which Bookchin endorses, distributes by need; primitivists favour sharing as in foraging bands.

production-for-use.rationale: They oppose profit-driven productivism and favour production for needs, in line with Kropotkin and Bookchin's critique of commodity relations.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Eco-anarchists link exploitation of labour to environmental damage and attack capitalist accumulation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Anarchists reject any dictatorial state, including a proletarian one.

collective-farming.rationale: Primitivists reject agriculture, while Kropotkin favoured communal horticulture and others favour small-scale local farming; split.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Anti-capitalists and anti-statists link states' competition and extraction to conflict, but the sources do not state the imperialism thesis.

taxation-theft.rationale: Anarchists reject the state but green anarchists, unlike libertarians, do not frame taxes as theft; unaddressed.

harm-principle.rationale: Anarchists reject state restriction but often accept communal sanctions; the sources do not address it.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Anarchists stress community and mutual aid; Bookchin favours communal relations, although individual freedom matters.

conscription.rationale: Inferred from the anarchist rejection of state coercion (s1); the sources do not discuss military conscription.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Anarchists favour both freedom to leave and direct participation; unaddressed.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred from the movement's anti-state and anti-capitalist stance (s1); the idea of running government as a business is not discussed.

positive-liberty.rationale: Social ecology and communist anarchism hold that freedom needs material conditions and Bookchin sees technology freeing people from toil; primitivists see freedom as wildness, so mild agreement.

media-academia-power.rationale: Anarchists see state and capital as dominant; unaddressed, though primitivists criticise mediated culture.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Inferred from Bookchin's opposition to hierarchy and domination (s4); the sources do not discuss genetic race differences.

organic-representation.rationale: Anarchists reject representation altogether, preferring direct participation in assemblies; the corporatist form is state-linked.

total-state.rationale: Total state control is the antithesis of anarchism.

national-rebirth.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of nations in favour of bioregions (s1); the sources do not discuss national rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Inferred from their opposition to states and empires (s1); territorial expansion is not discussed directly.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of hierarchy in Bookchin (s4); feudal oath-based rule is not discussed.

bound-labor.rationale: Inferred from the anarchist opposition to domination (s4); serfdom is not discussed directly.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Primitivists criticise science and technology as embodying domination, but Bookchin held that reason and ethics are universal; mild agreement inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: Bookchin held an objective, rational ethics rooted in thinking nature, while primitivists and postmodern-leaning strands distrust reason; split.

single-common-good.rationale: Anarchists reject a single authority defining the common good; Bookchin does use a rational ecological society, hence only mild disagreement.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Anarchists reject states, including nation-states founded on ethnic claims; unaddressed.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Right of return to a state is not an anarchist demand; inferred from anti-state stance.

revive-national-language.rationale: National revival under the state is not a goal, though they value local cultures; inferred.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Green syndicalism seeks self-management and councils in workplaces; anti-industrial strands would prefer abolishing large companies.

school-vouchers.rationale: Anarchists reject state schooling and its funding; vouchers keep it state-funded and market-based, so inferred disagreement.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is a state matter that anarchists do not address; no stated position.

economic-freedom.rationale: They reject capitalism but defend freedom from the state; the claim links freedom to markets, which splits their view.

rule-by-example.rationale: They reject rulers altogether, though they value moral example and prefigurative practice; inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Replace nation-states by bioregional and municipal communities; self-determination of communities, not nations, is the aim.

force-without-un.rationale: Inferred from their opposition to state militaries (s1); the sources do not discuss UN authorisation.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Bookchin champions reason, while primitivists criticise rationalism and deep ecology has spiritual elements; split.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: They reject state borders and the exclusion; inferred from anti-state, egalitarian outlook.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Primitivists and others oppose coerced labour and the work ethic; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: They oppose capitalist employers and favour class-conscious struggle (Bookchin), or abolition of work relations.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: They reject civilization's institutions but do not argue for destroying libraries and museums; unaddressed.

dominated-front.rationale: They reject state alliances but oppose Western-led globalised capitalism; unaddressed so inferred.

workers-nation.rationale: They reject nations and favour internationalist anarchism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Anarchism opposes patriarchy as hierarchy, and ecofeminists are part of the movement; primitivists see foraging societies as egalitarian.

ban-interest.rationale: They oppose usury as a capitalist practice, but legal bans need the state; unaddressed.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Inferred from anarchist egalitarianism and opposition to state hierarchy (s4); segregation laws are not discussed.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Many anarchists see the state as an instrument of domination, but Bookchin warns against equating hierarchy with class and state, and eco-anarchists tie states to extraction.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Green anarchists oppose extraction and have targeted fossil-fuel infrastructure.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: They reject national culture as a goal and nation-states; Bookchin criticises xenophobia.

elite-replacement.rationale: Inferred: the movement opposes borders and nationalism (s1), so it would reject this conspiracy theory, which the sources do not mention.

proportional-representation.rationale: Parliamentary representation is rejected in favour of direct democracy; inferred.

national-mission.rationale: Inferred from anti-statism (s1); exporting a form of government is not discussed.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of coercive hierarchy (s4); eugenics is not discussed.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Opposed to state violence, they would favour accountability, though they reject courts of the state; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Wikipedia places green anarchism within anarchism, which rejects all forms of hierarchy and authority; as in anarchism generally, even a minimal state is opposed.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Inferred from anarchist egalitarianism (s4); the sources do not discuss interracial marriage.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Anti-hierarchy but deep ecologists and total-liberation thinkers extend moral worth beyond humans and some reject the human-first framing, so mild agreement.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Marxist-Leninist debate outside the anarchist frame; no stated view.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Sympathy with indigenous peoples and critique of states and civilization imply it; inferred.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Uniform state law is state legislation; they would reject state law altogether.

restrict-conversion.rationale: State restriction of belief is state coercion that anarchists oppose.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Anarchists reject state schools, so the premise is not theirs; unaddressed.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Inferred: anarchists want the state abolished (s1), so they reject a socialist state growing stronger; the encirclement thesis itself is not discussed.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Anarchists want voluntary association, but reject that any government can be legitimate, even by consent; mild agreement.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist export aims are for state competitiveness and extraction that they oppose.

population-transfer.rationale: Inferred from their opposition to state coercion (s4); expulsions are not discussed.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: They embrace cooperation and mutual aid, drawing on Kropotkin and Bookchin's symbiosis, and criticise capitalism's grow-or-die competition.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: They reject the state's power to outlaw groups, being among the movements most affected.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Anarchists reject state coercion, yet green strands defend sabotage of property and direct action; they reject the absolutism.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Anti-hierarchy ethics make domination the central evil; Bookchin names hierarchy as a root problem.

separated-powers.rationale: Anarchists want no state; Bookchin favours confederation of assemblies, which is not separation of powers among state organs.

vanguard-party.rationale: Anarchists reject vanguard parties; Bookchin criticises hierarchy in the left and values popular assemblies.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Egalitarian outlook implies it but sources do not state it; inferred.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Home privatisation is not an anarchist aim; inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Green syndicalists favour strikes, workplace sabotage and linking labour and environmental movements.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Bookchin attributes crises to capitalism and hierarchy, not population; deep ecologists blame population for environmental, not poverty, problems.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Anarchists reject the premise; Bookchin criticises xenophobic closed societies.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Rejects elections and professional politicians but anarchists reject offices; sortition fits assembly models, inferred.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of state authority (s1); emergency powers are not discussed.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: State price setting uses state power; unaddressed.

party-controls-media.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of state and party domination (s1); media control is not discussed.

party-commands-army.rationale: They reject armies and ruling parties.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: State citizenship rules are not an anarchist concern; they oppose borders, inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: They reject representatives, but where such offices exist they favour mandated, modest-paid delegates; inferred.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Anarchists distrust party discipline though accept binding decisions of assemblies; mild disagreement.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: They reject supranational unions as superstates, though Bookchin favours confederations of communities, which is a different sort of union.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of state hierarchy (s1); the executive-legislature question is not discussed and the answer rejects state forces altogether.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Inferred from the anarchist rejection of hierarchy (s4); church governance is not discussed.

clerical-rule.rationale: Clerical rule is a hierarchy and a state.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Anarchists oppose interstate war and the traditional anarchist line is working-class internationalism; the sources do not discuss this precise stance.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Anarchists reject state censorship, though primitivists criticise mass culture.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: They reject presidents and state offices altogether.

recall-officials.rationale: Recallable, mandated delegates fit assembly democracy that Bookchin favours; they reject offices overall, hence mild agreement.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: They reject military alliances, bases and state armies; inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: They reject landlords but the legal ban is a state measure and communal housing is the aim; split and unaddressed.

people-in-arms.rationale: Some anarchist traditions favour popular militias, but green anarchists focus on direct action and many reject arms; unaddressed.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Primitivists and bioregionalists idealise life close to nature and criticise urban industrial society; Bookchin favours cities as sites of municipal democracy, hence mild.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of nation-states (s1); reunification is not discussed.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not addressed; some primitivists distrust intellectuals, but many adherents are themselves educated.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Primitivists reject the ranking of civilizations as progress; this is inferred from their critique of progress.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of state violence (s1); capital punishment is not discussed in the sources.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Anarchists reject state schooling, so the curriculum issue is not theirs; unaddressed.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Green anarchism draws on Darwin to reject anthropocentrism; they reject state schooling, so the question is mostly moot.

restrict-pornography.rationale: State restriction is disfavoured, though some ecofeminists oppose pornography; inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred: citizenship is a state category they reject and descent rules add ethnic exclusion (s1); not discussed directly.

minority-language-support.rationale: They value local and indigenous cultures but reject state programmes; inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Anarchists reject the state's laws so exemptions are not their issue; unaddressed.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Anarchism prizes freedom from conformity, but sources do not address Mill's claim; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Anti-capitalists oppose debt bondage and globalised finance; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anti-capitalism and anti-globalisation suggest it, but they are also anti-state; inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Assemblies appeal to them but a constitution is state-making; unaddressed.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Green anarchists reject economic growth and authoritarian rule (s1); trading freedom for development is not discussed as such.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Egalitarian but anti-development and anti-state; aid between states is not their issue.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred from their opposition to state militaries and to nuclear technology (s1); deterrence is not discussed.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: They reject heads of state altogether.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central banks are institutions of state and finance capital; they oppose both.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Nationalist land claims are rejected; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Their position is that private property should be abolished, so the common-good test is a weaker version; mild agreement.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Anarchists have long criticised the Soviet state; Bookchin critiques Marxism-Leninism, but the sources do not state the label.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmentalism favours precaution, but the question concerns governments; inferred.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred from their opposition to states and their militaries (s1); military alliances are not discussed.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Anarchists oppose annexation but not state boundaries as such; unaddressed.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: They oppose both church and state hierarchy, and would not empower the state; inferred.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from their support for community autonomy and opposition to state force (s1); secession is not discussed.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of rulers and hierarchy (s4); sacred kingship is not discussed.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Income tax is state revenue and flat rates favour the wealthy; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: Social ecology holds that domination is socially produced, but primitivists appeal to innate wildness; weakly inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of rulers (s4); the question of a ruler above the law is not discussed.

space-expansion.rationale: Inferred from the movement's critique of industrial technology and civilization (s1, s2); space colonisation is not discussed directly.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of rule by anyone (s1); constitutional design is not discussed.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of domination (s4); leader cults are not discussed.

equal-parenting.rationale: Unaddressed; state courts are not their instrument.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Marxist-Leninist debate; unaddressed in the sources.

land-redistribution.rationale: Anti-property and egalitarian, but they would favour common and rewilded land more than parcelling to farmers; inferred.

refugee-return.rationale: They oppose state expulsions, so they support return; inferred.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of nationalism and state expansion (s1); irredentism is not discussed.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of state coercion (s1); apostasy laws are not discussed.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of state coercion and patriarchy (s4); dress laws are not discussed.

common-currency.rationale: Supranational money is a feature of state and finance capital; they favour local exchange, inferred.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Ethnic unions of states are rejected.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Unaddressed; their stance on states makes both options state-based.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Bookchin's social ecology says hierarchy and domination drive crises, and primitivists stress agriculture and technology, partly material, partly cultural; split.

ban-cartels.rationale: State action to preserve competition conflicts with both anti-state and anti-market views; inferred.

no-bailouts.rationale: They oppose supporting capital with public money, though not through free-market reasoning; inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Anarchists reject courts and majority states, but Bookchin favours majority rule in assemblies; weak disagreement.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: They reject state bodies, though they oppose patriarchy; unaddressed.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Local self-reliance is valued but imperial blocs are state projects; split.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: They favour labour and environmental protection but oppose trade agreements and the state; split.

moral-incentives.rationale: Sharing and mutual aid replace material incentive in communist anarchist and foraging ideals; inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Insurrectionary and violent strands (Kaczynski, ITS) accept it, while Bookchin criticises individualist terrorism; split.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Hierarchy of any kind including inherited rank is rejected.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Nation or civilization-centred history is rejected by those who criticise civilization and nation-states.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: They support anti-racist remedies in principle; the state is not their agent; inferred.

public-money-creation.rationale: State money creation is a state function; unaddressed.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Eco-anarchists see capitalism as driving ecological collapse; Bookchin says grow-or-die imperative is unsustainable, so adaptation is doubted.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred from their opposition to state and imperial power (s1); post-imperial influence is not discussed.

delink-world-market.rationale: They oppose globalised capitalism and favour local self-reliance, though the focus is on communities, not poor countries; inferred.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Marxist debate not addressed in the sources.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Anarcho-capitalist; green anarchists oppose property rights framing and discrimination as domination.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: They reject constitutions and state-defined rights, but value liberties; inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Anti-colonial, and states and borders are rejected; inferred.

elective-rulers.rationale: Preferable to heredity but they reject rulers altogether.

minority-veto.rationale: Consensus-based anarchists accept individual vetoes, while Bookchin explicitly attacks consensus as a tyranny of structurelessness and favours majority decisions; split.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Resistance to rulers is natural for anarchists, though they would not stop at lawless ones; inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inference: the statement sets parliament against the monarch; anarchists reject both as state institutions (s4) and would refuse to make either supreme, but the choice between them is not discussed.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anti-fascist, but they reject constitutions; mild agreement inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anarchists oppose authoritarianism of both sorts, though many reject the equivalence framing; inferred.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred from their egalitarian principles (s4); the sources do not discuss the causes of the American Civil War.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Anarchists oppose patriarchy but not the programme; unaddressed.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: They reject Western state institutions, but not as a civilisational relativism; primitivists criticise civilization generally.

paid-care-work.rationale: Ecofeminists note unpaid care work, but wages are rejected; split.

filial-duty.rationale: Anti-hierarchy outlook is against enforced deference; inferred.

office-by-exam.rationale: They reject officials, state bureaucracies and specialisation.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Anti-capitalism but not state protectionism; inferred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Free association is the anarchist principle, so ending marriages without fault; inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Bookchin's confederalism keeps delegates answerable to assemblies; anarchist federalism uses mandated, recallable delegates.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Financialised private accounts are capitalist and the state's pension is also rejected; they favour mutual aid.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Community ownership is a stated eco-anarchist principle and use-based holding fits Kropotkin; primitivists reject ownership altogether.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: They reject budgets and states; inferred.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal liberation and total liberation are central concerns, with Reclus linking cruelty to animals and exploitation of labour.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Total liberation and ALF actions reject animal use; primitivists accept hunting, so only moderate disagreement.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: They reject class privilege and charity from elites in favour of mutual aid; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Primitivists and lifestyle strands favour withdrawal, but most adherents emphasise direct action and Bookchin criticises apolitical withdrawal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Zerzan's critique treats symbolic culture, mediated life and time discipline as alienating; sources show this as a primitivist view.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Unaddressed; Zerzan's critique of culture suggests yes but sources are not explicit.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Anti-globalisation and anti-extraction stance suggests it; inferred.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Local self-sufficiency is valued; the state framing is not theirs; inferred.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Anarchists reject political leadership by any group, though they respect indigenous land authority.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Primitivists seek a moneyless foraging life and the eco-anarchist case for degrowth and communal ownership points the same way, but Bookchin's communism is less explicit about money; mild agreement.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: They oppose central banks as state-capital institutions but reject leaving money to the market; the statement's market framing splits the answer.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Bookchin lists patriarchy among the hierarchies behind ecological crisis and ecofeminism is part of green anarchism; sources state it as hierarchy rather than a systematic claim.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Anarchists see rulers as inherently corrupting, though the sources do not state the claim in these terms; inferred.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Total liberation vegans oppose slaughter but reject state bans, and primitivists accept hunting; split.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Primitivism rejects the idea that civilization is an improvement, and anarchists reject rule over others.

single-official-language.rationale: Anarchists reject the state imposing a common language and favour decentralised, communal self-determination; this is inferred from the anti-state and decentralist principles.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Green anarchists reject nationalism and state border control, and want land held communally rather than by nations; a citizens-only land rule is inferred to be opposed.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Anarchists oppose hierarchy and structural domination but also state regulatory remedies, and the sources do not address the question, so the strands are taken as split.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The critique of capitalism, industrial production and growth, with degrowth as a goal, treats mass consumption as destructive of nature and of human life.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Opposition to the state, militarism and imperial power politics means a state arming proxy forces to weaken rivals is rejected.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Anti-state, anti-hierarchical and decentralist, green anarchists reject a great power forcing its allies into line by invasion.

corporate-influence.rationale: Green anarchists hold that capitalism and states together drive ecological destruction, so corporate capture of government is a core grievance.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Anarchists reject state power over civil society and nationalism, so state limits on funding for sovereignty are opposed.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Anarchists oppose state engineering of families, and population growth is seen as an ecological problem by many strands.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local control and bioregionalism appeal, but it would give authorities coercive power; inferred, and strands may differ.

job-guarantee.rationale: The state acting as employer cuts against abolishing both state and wage labour; primitivists reject industrial work altogether.

democratic-peace.rationale: Representative democracy is seen as another form of state domination, so spreading it is not treated as a route to peace; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Rejecting the state as illegitimate hierarchy implies no inherent duty to obey its laws.

non-intervention.rationale: Anarchists oppose state wars and imperialism, but also reject state sovereignty as such; the literal "no right" claim is inferred.

industrial-unions.rationale: Green syndicalists support industrial unionism, while primitivists reject industry and unions; the strands split.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Anarchist egalitarianism and anti-nationalism reject conspiracy scapegoating of a minority.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Anarchists reject state-conferred institutions, so state-backed marriage is inferred to be opposed.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Anarchists distrust state secrecy, though they do not seek to strengthen state law; inferred.

local-production.rationale: Decentralised, bioregional and communal economies are central to the family, and global industrial trade is the target of its critique.

informal-organisation.rationale: Affinity groups and direct action are favoured, especially by primitivists, while social ecologists prefer federations; the mainstream is leaning informal.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Anarchists reject both national and international state authority, so neither takes precedence.

religious-nation.rationale: Anarchism rejects both nationalism and religious authority, so a creed-defined nation is opposed.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Anarchism rejects hierarchy and the state, so ritual submission to a leading power is opposed.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Bioregional decentralization favors local control, but mutual aid between communities argues for sharing; strands differ.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Social ecologists and anarcho-communists favor common productive resources with personal items private; primitivists dispute property altogether.

defeat-communism.rationale: Green anarchists oppose state communism as a hierarchy but do not call for defeating it; inferred.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Rejection of the state and capitalism implies communal rather than state or private provision; inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: Bookchin's wing is secular, while some green anarchists embrace spiritual or pagan ideas, so they split.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Green anarchism holds capitalism drives ecological destruction, though Bookchin credits it with material abundance; primitivists reject any such view.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anti-hierarchy politics includes anarcha-feminism; a link to ending economic hierarchy is inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: Communal care fits communal societies, but primitivists reject specialized services; adherents split.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Anti-nationalism and anti-state positions make official language purging unlikely; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Adherents back indigenous peoples but reject state treaties as state instruments; they split.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Stateless, communal, bioregional societies are the family's core vision.

majority-settlement.rationale: Anti-state and anti-nationalist views oppose state-steered settlement; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Anarchism presents itself as a stateless path distinct from both capitalism and state communism; inferred.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred from anarchist hostility to nationalism and states, though green anarchists support Indigenous land defence.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Anarchists have a long anti-fascist tradition and treat denial as a fascist falsehood.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Anarchists reject state control over personal life and sexuality.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Anarchism opposes state repression and demands free association as a basic principle.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Anarchists oppose both state power and religious authority, so state punishment of blasphemy is doubly rejected.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Anarchists oppose states and empires and their exploitation of peoples.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: anarchists back resistance to invasion but reject religious obligation and military organisation.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Anarchists reject religious authority and any rulers claiming divine law as legitimacy.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Direct, face-to-face decision making in communities and workplaces is central, e.g. Bookchin's libertarian municipalism.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Bookchin's social ecology traces ecological ruin to interlocking hierarchies and domination, though primitivists focus on civilisation itself.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from anarchist opposition to imposed social hierarchies, including gender; the texts are not specific, and some primitivists dissent.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from anarchist emphasis on bodily autonomy against state control; the texts do not address it.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Inferred: green anarchists see themselves as an anti-authoritarian left and attack both camps' statism, though some call themselves beyond left and right.

alienated-labor.rationale: Primitivists and social ecologists both criticise work under civilisation and capitalism as alienating and domesticating.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Anarchists oppose nativism and cultural essentialism.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Inferred from the anarchist rejection of all claims to political authority (s1, s3); divine right is not discussed directly.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred: anarchists oppose religion and state coercion alike, so there is no common view.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred: anarchists distrust both employers and the courts and the state, so there is no clear stance.

social-market-economy.rationale: Green anarchists reject both market capitalism and the state that would regulate it.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Abolition of the state implies abolition of its armies, and green anarchism opposes militarism.

rich-first.rationale: Anarchists reject hierarchy and trickle-down development as legitimising inequality.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred from anarchist opposition to states, militarism and great-power alliances.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Green anarchism rejects hierarchy and the state, so hereditary rule is an extreme case of what it opposes.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the anarchist tradition's mutualist, self-managed alternatives to profit-making banks.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from its anti-state, anti-capitalist stance: lenders' conditions are rejected, though it also rejects the state that borrows.

property-franchise.rationale: It rejects both the state and class hierarchy, so a wealth-based vote is opposed, though it also rejects voting itself.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Green anarchism includes social ecology and total liberation, which treat all domination, of people and of nature, as linked.

reification.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from its critique of capitalism and of civilization's alienation, though strands differ.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the anarchist critique that capital controls communication, though some reject formal institutions entirely.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Anarchists reject rule by the state as such, so standing state laws are no remedy, though they oppose arbitrary rule. Inferred, and strands differ.

racial-franchise.rationale: Its opposition to hierarchy and domination rules out racial limits on political rights.

online-participation.rationale: Social ecologists favor direct democracy and could use online tools, while primitivists reject technology, so the strands split.

open-government-data.rationale: Not addressed; open records fit direct democracy but anarchists reject state governance, so the strands are split.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Its anti-authority stance opposes state restriction of marriage, and its anti-hierarchy stance opposes communal exclusion.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Its anti-hierarchy stance opposes singling out people for domination or exclusion by religion.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Green anarchists favour direct, face-to-face and assembly-based decision-making over representation, which sits close to citizen assemblies, though lot selection is not discussed; inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Anarchists oppose religious authority, but whether to reform doctrine or reject it outright is not addressed and strands differ.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Anarchists oppose capitalism and concentrated economic power as hierarchies that dominate people, and both social ecologists and primitivists criticise them.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Anarchists reject armies and the state, so most would not endorse military service at all, though they oppose discrimination; inferred.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Anarchists reject the state's use of schools to impose any doctrine, and stateless society has no such institution.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Anarchism rejects the state and its coercive institutions, and green anarchists want stateless societies; Bookchin's wing keeps communal defence but not state police.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Anarchists reject state executive offices altogether, preferring confederated assemblies; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Anarchists reject state aid but favour mutual aid and communal provision over charity, so the statement fits only partly.

term-limits.rationale: Anarchists reject government office rather than limit it; inferred, with assembly-based rotation of delegates as one related practice.

vote-delegation.rationale: Bookchin's assemblies and confederations use mandated, recallable delegates, but anarchists generally reject voting as representation; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed; primitivists and social ecologists disagree on technology, and the focus is on ecological and social crisis.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the anti-hierarchy stance, though many reject religious institutions.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Anarchism opposes hierarchy including patriarchal authority in the household, so equal spouses fit its principles.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the anarchist rejection of borders and favouring of local, community self-government by all residents.

rent-control.rationale: Anarchists reject state regulation but support tenant and community control of housing, so adherents are split on a legal cap.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from the anarchist opposition to property and capitalism, though the sources do not address patents.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from the anarchist rejection of the state, nationalism and military discipline.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the anarchist opposition to states and the ecological opposition to nuclear technology.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the anarchist opposition to states and militaries.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the anarchist opposition to states, though they would not want the state to be the one recognising.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Anarchism opposes capitalism and hierarchy, and the sources describe a critique of capitalism as a driver of destruction, so income should follow work, not ownership.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents split between pacifists and those who accept defensive or direct-action violence.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from the anarchist rejection of nationalism and the state.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; green anarchists have no shared position on this feminist-theory question.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the anarchist rejection of fixed hierarchy and categories.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from the anarchist rejection of the state and nationalism.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred from the secular, anti-authoritarian tradition, which rejects holy-war framings of politics.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the tradition rejects national homelands more than it designs them.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred from the anarchist rejection of nationalism, though cultural change is stressed by primitivists.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents are split between secular and pagan or spiritual strands.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the anarchist opposition to hierarchy, including patriarchy.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from the anarchist rejection of nationalism and ethnic hierarchy.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from the anarchist rejection of state territorial administration and nationalism.

independent-unions.rationale: Anarchists reject state control of unions and favour free workers' organisation such as green syndicalism, but primitivists reject industrial labour altogether.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Anarchists reject state ownership as not socialist and insist on power in the hands of the people directly; primitivists reject the framing, so the answer is moderate.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Anarchists reject state ownership but favour communal control of local services; primitivists reject modern infrastructure, so strands split.

second-chamber.rationale: Anarchists reject legislatures and states; a second chamber of any kind is a further layer of governing hierarchy.

municipal-property.rationale: Social ecology favours municipal ownership through the commune and the assembly, while primitivists favour common land; neither accepts private or state ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Bookchin's social ecology and confederalism hold that assemblies decide and confederal delegates only coordinate, and anarchists reject binding central authority generally.

family-wage.rationale: Not addressed; anarchists reject wage labour and the state so a statutory family wage does not fit, but communal support for households is common.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed; social ecologists favour communal medicine while primitivists question modern medicine, so strands split.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred from the primitivist critique of technological civilisation and acceptance of natural life cycles, though social ecologists are less opposed.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from the anarchist rejection of state control of money and surveillance; primitivists reject money altogether.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the anarchist opposition to state surveillance and identification and the tradition of anonymous direct action.

person-over-state.rationale: Anarchists put the individual above the state, but social ecology treats the person as embedded in community and ecology, and primitivists reject humanist framings; strands split.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Some primitivists and deep ecology currents stress spiritual and animist bonds with nature, while social ecologists and most anarchists are secular; strands split.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Anarchists reject the state, so a national legislature holding final authority contradicts their position; inferred.

gm-crops.rationale: Primitivists reject domestication and technology, and green anarchists broadly oppose genetically engineered crops and agribusiness; social ecologists are also critical.

dense-cities.rationale: Primitivists want to dissolve cities, and social ecologists favour smaller human-scale communities in bioregions; adherents largely reject mass urbanism.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Anarchists reject group-based identity politics of states and nations; inferred from the anti-hierarchical, universalist stance.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from the anti-nationalist and anti-hierarchical stance of anarchism.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Anarchists oppose the state's wars and militaries and favour defensive volunteer resistance; inferred from anti-militarism.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Anarchists reject the nation-state and nationhood as a basis of identity; green anarchists favour bioregional and communal units over national ones.

communal-electorates.rationale: Green anarchists reject representative electoral politics altogether, so separate religious electorates are not something they would support.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred from anarchist rejection of nationalism: they see no 'my country' to defend and blame states and capital, not foreign plots, for harm.

free-public-college.rationale: Bookchin's social anarchists favour free education but not through the state, while primitivists reject schooling and civilization; the strands split.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred: green anarchists see ecological harm as rooted in capitalism and the state, so state-run taxes and market fixes are seen as reforms that entrench both; they prefer abolition or direct action.

future-generations.rationale: Ecological survival for coming generations is the core concern of the tradition; Wikipedia's overview presents the destruction of the environment as the driving critique.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Ecofeminist strands link women to care and nature, but social ecologists and many anarchists reject gender essentialism; the family is split.

arms-reduction.rationale: Anarchists oppose militaries and war, but 'consistent with national safety' presupposes a state and nation; inferred agreement with the aim only.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Anarchists reject state diplomacy altogether, so openness within it is not their question; inferred from their rejection of the state.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred: green anarchists reject capitalism but also state control, so would not hand the state this power, though some favour localising economies.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Green anarchism rejects the state and its monopoly on force, so it would not leave arms to state forces alone.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: As anti-state and anti-militarist anarchists they back refusal of state wars, though some strands accept armed resistance.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Green syndicalists favour unions while primitivists reject wage labour altogether, so the strands split.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: State top-ups prop up wage labour and the state, both of which they reject; inferred from anti-state, anti-capitalist principles.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Legal fiscal rules are state instruments; inferred disapproval from the anti-state stance, though they also oppose debt-driven growth.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: They want to abolish states and capitalism rather than reform global rules, though they sympathise with poorer countries; not addressed.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The anarchist core is abolishing the state and replacing it with stateless, decentralised, communal forms, not capturing it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Anarchists reject fixed blueprints and favour decentralised, bioregional or communal experiments; Bookchin's confederal plans are a mild exception.

nature-as-capital.rationale: They blame capitalism and the market for ecological destruction and treat putting a price on nature as part of that commodification.

sacred-nation.rationale: Anarchists reject nationalism and the state, so a sacred nation is firmly rejected.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from anti-capitalist hostility to debt and finance, though a state cancellation runs against anti-state principle.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Their critique of hierarchy and capitalism makes core-periphery exploitation a natural claim; inferred, not stated.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Primitivists reject domestication and civilisation's shaping of people while social ecologists affirm a common humanity; adherents split.

public-service-media.rationale: State-funded media conflicts with anti-state principle, though they also oppose commercial media control; inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Anarchists mostly reject organised religion as hierarchy, though primitivists and some strands admire animist traditions; the question is not addressed in the sources.

farm-price-support.rationale: Green anarchists reject state intervention, and primitivists reject commercial agriculture itself; inferred from anti-statism.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Green anarchists reject the state and industrial technology, and nuclear weapons are the extreme of both; inferred from those positions.

workers-own-party.rationale: Anarchists reject party politics and the state it would seek to win, so a workers' party is refused as a hierarchical vehicle.

ban-fgm.rationale: Anarchists oppose the practice but also reject state criminal law, and primitivists defend traditional societies, so adherents split.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Anarchism opposes patriarchy and hierarchy, so equal property rights are favoured, though some reject property title altogether; inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Decentralised, bioregional communities would name their own speech; no state would impose a single standard. Inferred from decentralism.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Green anarchists reject agencies and courts alike, and favour direct action and community sanction against polluters; a lawsuit regime is inferred as unwelcome.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Chiefs are hierarchy backed by custom, which anarchists oppose, though they admire some stateless indigenous societies; inferred from anti-hierarchy.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Adherents split: ecological priority is central, but freedom is the anarchist core and coercive priority by a state is rejected.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Anarchists reject the state's punishment system and fixed state sentencing; inferred from anti-statism.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Anarchists reject state requirements and borders; inferred from anti-statism.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Anarchists favour voluntary and independent worker organisation, but green anarchists are split on unions and compulsory membership is not discussed.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred: anarchists reject state control of identity and exclusion from participation, so they would oppose state ID requirements for voting.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the anarchist rejection of state establishment of any religion.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Green anarchists reject representative government and elections as rule by a hierarchy; democracy for them is direct and assembly-based, not a procedure for choosing rulers.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from the anarchist rejection of state and religious control over personal life.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anarchists reject state authority over people and its use of repression to maintain order, so shutdowns by governments are rejected.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Anarchists reject state welfare administration and market capitalism alike, and favour mutual aid; a state cash scheme is not part of that, though it is not discussed.

women-suffrage.rationale: Anarchist opposition to hierarchy and domination extends to gender; the overview describes the tradition as opposed to all forms of domination, though suffrage itself is a state institution.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Anarchists oppose hierarchy including patriarchal religion, but sources show no shared view that religion is a major cause of women's oppression.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the anarchist and social-ecology opposition to racial hierarchy; not discussed on this specific claim.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred: anarchists oppose creating state bodies, even for good ends, and favour grassroots action.

missingStatements.text: Humanity should abandon agriculture and return to a hunter-gatherer way of life.
missingStatements.rationale: Anarcho-primitivists name agriculture as the origin of hierarchy and want it dissolved, though Bookchin's wing rejects this.
missingStatements.declined: Covered by return-to-foraging, which this audit answers 0 because anarcho-primitivists want agriculture abandoned but Bookchin-style social ecologists reject it.

missingStatements.text: Illegal sabotage of machinery and infrastructure is justified to protect wild nature.
missingStatements.rationale: Earth First! monkeywrenching and ELF actions against deforestation, roadbuilding and pipelines are central to the movement's direct-action tradition.

missingStatements.text: Large areas of land should be returned to wilderness and left free of human management.
missingStatements.rationale: Rewilding is part of primitivist practice and deep ecology's biocentrism in green anarchism.

notes: The largest internal splits are primitivism versus Bookchin's social ecology (foraging, technology, consensus, population control). Several 0 answers record that split or the movement's silence on a state-policy question.
